title: IdP fingerprinting & connector test matrix for SSO (Okta/Azure/Google/Ping)
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Create a canonical IdP fingerprint and connector test matrix covering Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping to validate SAML behaviors that affect RBAC v2 mappings and audit logging. Produce test harnesses, run coverage against existing connectors, and document required console admin controls and fallbacks.
scope: This ticket focuses on empirically enumerating IdP-specific behaviors that change SAML assertions or binding flows in ways that affect: attribute/group-based role mapping, NameID formats, encrypted vs signed assertions, ACS/RelayState handling, and audit log fidelity. It does NOT change runtime code except for small test-only flags and visibility hooks. Work will deliver a test matrix, pass/fail results, recommended mitigations, and a draft admin-facing doc for Console controls.
decisions: Use a common test harness that can replay SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows against each IdP emulator and a short-term real tenant in each IdP for validation.
Map RBAC v2 role assignment to use both group claim and a fallback attribute claim; implement deterministic precedence ordering documented in Console.
Audit logs will include raw SAML NameID, major attribute claims used for RBAC decisions, and a normalized idp_source tag to help cross-tenant debugging.
tradeoffs: Recording raw SAML attributes in audit logs increases storage/retention costs but improves root cause analysis for SSO failures.
Implementing IdP-specific workarounds increases maintenance burden; prefer generic fallbacks where possible and document IdP edge cases clearly for admins.
Aggressive normalization of group names risks masking user intent when IdP conveys organization-specific prefixes; normalization will be conservative.
test_matrix: Okta: SAML 2.0 default NameID (emailAddress) vs transient; group claim via Groups -> token; test encrypted assertions and SHA-256 signatures.
Azure AD: group overage behavior (hasGroups=true + Graph API PST); test case for nested groups and claim size truncation via 'hasgroups' flow.
Google Workspace: SAML attribute mapping quirks when using delegated admin vs domain-level mapping; test non-standard attribute aliases.
Ping: support for multiple ACS URLs, RelayState strictness, and behavior when assertions are signed but not the response.
Cross-IdP: SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated RelayState preservation and effect on RBAC mapping flow.
test_plan: Build a small saml-tester harness (docker-compose) that can act as SP and replay signed/encrypted assertions. Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/saml-tester (PR: #582).
Provision ephemeral dev tenants in each IdP or use vendor-provided dev orgs where possible (Okta dev org, Azure test tenant, GSuite dev, Ping test instance).
Run 40 canonical scenarios per IdP (nameid formats, signed-response vs signed-assertion, encrypted assertion, group claim size, nested groups, RelayState edge cases, ACS mismatch).
Capture middleware-level logs annotated with idp_source, raw_saml_blob (truncated to 8k), and normalized_claims used by RBAC v2.
acceptance_criteria: A completed matrix with pass/fail for all canonical scenarios for each IdP and supporting evidence (saml-tester logs, screenshots or HAR files).
A short mitigation playbook per failing case listing recommended admin console settings and any short-term runtime flags.
Console doc draft describing admin-facing controls for role precedence, attribute fallbacks, and audit log toggles.
Security review sign-off recorded in ticket comments and PR description.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created; initial scoping and PR for saml-tester repo opened (draft).
2025-02-20: Okta dev org provisioned; initial tests show Okta returns group names prefixed with application label when using 'Group' claim -> need normalization rule. Added to tradeoffs.
2025-02-26: Azure AD tests show hasGroups overage behavior — group claim replaced with 'hasgroups' boolean if user is in >150 groups. Added fallback flow to test_plan to exercise Graph lookup path.

2025-03-03: Ran Google Workspace attribute alias tests; discovered admin console mapping can emit attrs with different key casing. Implemented case-insensitive claim lookup in normalization. Added note for Console doc.

2025-03-08: Ping instance returned signed-assertion but unsigned-response in one test; audit log lacked assertion-level signature tag — changed logging hook to capture assertion signature validation result.
review_feedback: PM review (Riley Morgan): Recommend adding an explicit section for how SCIM provisioning and JIT account creation interact with RBAC v2 mappings.
Design review (Leah Chen): Console controls should expose 'preview' mode to show role mapping results before commit. Add wireframes to Confluence.
Security review (Devon Brooks): Must redact PII in stored saml blobs; store only hashed identifiers and the normalized claims used for RBAC decisions.
recommendations: Expose 'Role Mapping Preview' in Console to allow admins to test a sample SAML response against configured mappings without affecting live users.
Default RBAC v2 precedence: explicit user attribute > group claim > SCIM-provisioned groups > JIT defaults. Document precedence clearly.
Add a Console toggle 'Audit SAML Details' (opt-in per org) with TTL-based retention and clear redaction guidance.
notes: This artifact should be used as the engineering canonical for IdP oddities that influence RBAC v2 and audit expectations. The next step after acceptance is a separate ticket to implement any runtime fallback code paths deemed necessary (e.g., Graph lookup for Azure overage).
final_comment: Next: demo to security and PM with live preview and sample tenant; prepare release notes for security-2025.03.
implementation_notes: Keep saml raw blob retention configurable per-org via Console (default off).
Implement normalized_claims extractor as a small library used by Console and runtime to ensure mapping parity.
Avoid IdP-specific hard-coded rules unless absolutely necessary; favor documented fallbacks.
